linkedin_post:
Monday we're publishing the episode behind a stat that's been sitting with us for weeks:

Between 2017 and 2022, the number of US software companies with fewer than five employees grew 55%. They're now the majority of software publishers in the country.

Nobody covered a single one of them.

We pulled the Census data, the app-store economics, and a handful of company-level numbers most people haven't seen put next to each other. Some of it is very good news. Some of it is a genuinely uncomfortable stat about what a typical attempt is worth right now.

Both are true at the same time, which is exactly why nobody tells this story cleanly.

Episode drops Monday at 11:00 AM ET.
